key_insight: ReuF2F benchmarks coding agents on formalized undergraduate-level open research problems, with the best evaluated model resolving only about 40%.
engineering_relevance: Lean 4 verification and a containerized coding-agent workflow provide a practical testbed for machine-checkable mathematical problem solving.
method: Formalize 244 REU open problems across diverse mathematical subfields in Lean 4.
Place each problem and its logical negation in a Lean project inside a Docker container.
Use Leanimum-agent, built on mini-SWE-agent, as a unified evaluation harness.
evidence_signal: Across the 244-problem benchmark, the best-performing evaluated model resolves approximately 40% of problems.
watch_item: Less prominent problems may reduce solution exposure, but their long-term suitability for held-out evaluation remains uncertain.
paper_title: ReuF2F: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Formalized Undergraduate Research Problems
